The Ladder, Tags, Marks, Sensors and Log tabs, and what every control on them does.

The window

The main tab RimPLC sits on the bottom bar. Its header carries the scan rate and the Notices switch; below it, five tabs.

Header

ControlWhat it does
- / +Halve or double the scan interval (60 to 2500 ticks). A faster scan reads the colony more often and costs more time per tick.
NoticesWhen ticked, a rung's notice is posted as a game message on its rising edge. Untick to keep the ladder silent and read it yourself.

Ladder

Every rung, one row each, in priority order. Each contact in the row is drawn by its state:

ColourMeaning
greenthe condition holds
darkit does not
amberthe reading it needs is unmeasured -- the game cannot give it, or the mod or expansion it names is not loaded
redunresolved: the condition names something nothing writes

A rung is live when every contact is green. The first live rung is the colony's job now.

ControlWhat it does
Live rungs onlyHide every rung that does not hold right now.
All familiesFilter the list by family: setup, survival, war, economy, research, base-and-fortress, animals, growth, configuration, royalty, ideology-biotech-anomaly, space, endgame, meta, start, backrooms.
Letters seenMark every letter on the stack as read, so letters drops to zero and an unread threat letter stops vouching.
New rungOpen the editor on an empty rung of your own.
EditOpen the editor on the selected rung. Editing a preset rung makes a player copy under the same id; the preset is not changed.
Remove / RevertRemove your own rung, or drop your copy of a preset rung so the preset's version returns.
Export / ImportSee Presets and building.
on / offSwitch a rung off and it is skipped. Switching a preset rung off is an owner action when the owner route is used (Commands).
advise / autoadvise (default): the rung only shows and posts its notice. auto: its coils run -- a message, a mark or a tag. Nothing else is ever executed.

Select a rung to read its then steps, its never list and its why -- the reason it exists, usually in the words of whoever asked for it.

The rung editor

Rows of key / operator / value. The key picker searches the sensors, the marks, the tags and the game's own definitions -- items, buildings, research projects and alert classes -- so a rung can read count_Steel, research_Gunsmithing or alert_ColonistNeedsRescue without those being pre-registered. A definition from a DLC or another mod adds a requires entry so the rung stays quiet when that content is absent.

Instructions (OR, NOT, timers, counters, one-shots) are edited as JSON from templates. Saving runs the same rules the repository's checker runs: unique ids, a numeric priority, every key a sensor, mark, tag or definition, every condition a value the key's type can satisfy.

Tags

Two lists. Variables are setpoints you may override within their min..max: food comfort days, the steel reserve, the colonist target. Constants are the owner's safety limits and change only through the owner route. Set writes an override, Clear returns to the preset value.

Marks

Named booleans and numbers for judgements the game cannot measure -- a camp declared stable, which kind of raid the last letter described, how many gate sections are done. Set, Clear and Add for a new one. A boolean mark never set reads false; a numeric mark reads its documented default.

Sensors

Every reading by group -- Game, World, Colony, Threats, Crew, Health, Food, Stores, Rooms, Power, Defence, Production, Research, Stream -- with its value and a tooltip saying what it means and when it warns. A warnings panel at the top lists the readings that are a problem right now (critical in red, warning in amber); Warnings only hides the rest. Critical warnings also raise an alert in RimWorld's own alert column.

The tab also lists every input a rung asks for that nothing is writing, with host inputs (readings pushed from outside the game) marked as such.

Log

The notices posted and the outputs recorded, newest first.

RimPLC. A development build; nothing here is a balance, performance or compatibility report.
